method: The absolute difference between the current and target stitch counts is the number of shaping groups. Divide the current stitches by that group count: every group receives the integer quotient, and the remainder is distributed one extra original stitch at a time using cumulative Bresenham-style rounding, so group sizes differ by at most one and their sum always equals the current count. For M1, the listed knit or purl stitches are followed by the increase, which consumes no original stitch. KFB reserves one original stitch for the shaping operation; k2tog and ssk reserve two. The remaining group stitches are worked as knit or purl before that operation. Identical adjacent instructions are compressed into repeat counts. One-row mode permits at most one shaping action per original-stitch group: increases cannot exceed the current count, and the target of a decrease cannot be below half the current count rounded up. No-change input produces an instruction to work every stitch.
